# Public, shape-only lock for scripts/check-forbidden.ps1 and the CI
# step that runs it. Every pattern below matches a generic shape (a
# Windows user-profile path, a Steam library layout, a workshop content
# folder, an absolute non-fixture drive path, a plan
# citation) and identifies no specific mod or person.
#
# Maintainers may keep additional project-specific patterns in a local,
# gitignored `.journal/forbidden-tokens.local.txt`; the script merges
# the two when that file is present. CI has no local file, so it runs
# this list alone. Lines starting with `#` are ignored by the script.
SteamLibrary
C:\\Users\\[a-z]{2,}
steamapps\\workshop\\content\\294100\\[0-9]
\bF:\\
\bD:\\
# Plan citations: public code states a rule, it never points at a design
# document that is not published. Each pattern matches the shape of a
# citation, not a topic, in any file and any context (code, string
# literal, `#` comment, markdown prose, config): a numbered-decision label
# (E14, E3), the plan's own label (R1/Q4), "the plan's ...",
# "item 2's"/"(item 6)", a section sign with a number, a
# provisional-decision id (PD-5-1), or a path into the journal's design
# docs. The uppercase shapes are case-sensitive on purpose, so a test's
# `r1` mod, a hex `e12` or the word `e2e` stays legal.
(?-i)\bE[0-9]{1,2}\b
# A label standing alone: not `"R1"` as a whole quoted value (test row
# ids), but `R1`, `R1's` and `"R1 is ..."` all count.
(?-i)\b[QR][1-9](\b[^"']|'s|$)
the plan's
\bitem [0-9]+(\)|'s)
# A section sign directly after a number is a standards citation
# ("RFC 9110 §15.4", "ISO 8601 §4", "ECMA-262 §7.1") and passes; any other
# section sign with a number is a pointer into an unpublished document.
(^|[^0-9,\s])\s*§[0-9]
(?-i)\bPD-[0-9]
\.journal/docs/[a-z0-9-]+\.md
-plan\.md
